questions.text: According to Text 1, why is Almaty more cosmopolitan than other cities?
opts: It has international connections and many cultures
questions.correct: It has international connections and many cultures
questions.hint: "Almaty is larger, louder, and more cosmopolitan... It has more international connections."

questions.text: Amir says Astana is more comfortable to live in than Almaty.
questions.hint: "Astana is more impressive than Almaty, but it's also less comfortable." — Amir.

questions.text: In Text 2, which factor does Amir say is more important than modern buildings?
questions.hint: "Better access to professors is worth more than a better-looking building."

questions.text: Kamila says the most significant factor in choosing a university is ___ .
questions.hint: "The most significant factor was not rank or fame, but fit."

questions.text: What does Text 1 say is the most honest definition of academic success?
opts: Getting a degree from the most prestigious place
questions.hint: "not the degree from the most famous institution, but the student who leaves four years later knowing exactly who they are."

questions.text: Text 2 admits that prestigious universities help with job prospects.
questions.hint: "a degree from a more famous university opens more doors in the job market. This is undeniably true."

questions.text: Which flat is closer to the university?
questions.hint: "Flat A is much closer — about eight minutes on foot. Flat B is at least twenty-five minutes by bus."

questions.text: Which flat has better natural light?
questions.hint: "Flat B has much better natural light." Flat A faces north and is darker.

questions.text: Kamila says "___ is harder to get back than sunlight."
questions.hint: "Time is harder to get back than sunlight." — Kamila's argument for Flat A despite the lighting.

questions.text: Flat A is on a busier, noisier street than Flat B.
questions.hint: "Flat B is noisier — it's right on the main road." / "Flat A is residential. Much more peaceful."

questions.text: Which flat has a more reliable landlord?
questions.hint: "The landlord seems more reliable too." — Zhibek about Flat A.

questions.text: What is Kamila's overall recommendation?
opts: Flat B because of the light
questions.hint: "Zhibek, it sounds like Flat A is the obvious choice — except for the light."

questions.text: "Big" comparative is:
questions.hint: "big" = CVC → double g + er: bigger. ✅

questions.text: "Beautiful" superlative is:
questions.hint: "beautiful" = 3+ syllables → the most beautiful. Always "the" before superlatives. ✅

questions.text: "good → ___ (comparative)" and "good → ___ (superlative)"
questions.hint: "good → better (comparative) → the best (superlative)" — both irregular.

questions.text: "She is ___ student in the class." (superlative of "dedicated")
questions.hint: "dedicated" = 4 syllables → the most dedicated. ✅

questions.text: "Flat A is ___ closer than Flat B." (BIG difference)
questions.hint: "much + comparative" = big difference. "Flat A is much closer." ✅

questions.text: "Almaty is the most bigger city in Kazakhstan" is correct.
questions.hint: ✅ "Almaty is the biggest city." — NEVER "the most" + short adjective. ✗ "the most bigger"!

questions.text: "Is this flat ___ nice ___ the other one?" (equal comparison)
questions.hint: "as + adjective + as" = equal comparison. "Is it AS NICE AS...?" ✅

questions.text: "Noisy" comparative is:
questions.hint: "noisy" ends in -y → drop y + ier: noisier. ✅ (Note: "the noisiest" is superlative, not comparative)

questions.text: "Almaty is the most cosmopolitan city." "Cosmopolitan" means:
questions.hint: "cosmopolitan" = including diverse cultures, people, and international influences.

questions.text: The teaching quality here is ___ higher than at larger universities.
questions.hint: "consistently" = always, over time. Not just sometimes — reliably always higher.

questions.text: "She felt invisible at the large university." This means:
questions.hint: "Invisible" here = not seen as an individual; anonymous and unnoticed.

questions.text: "The professor-to-student ratio is better here." "Ratio" means:
opts: The relationship in number between two things
questions.correct: The relationship in number between two things
questions.hint: "ratio" = the comparative relationship between two quantities, e.g. 1 professor : 15 students.

questions.text: "On paper, the option looked better." "On paper" means:
questions.hint: "on paper" = theoretically, based on written information, before experiencing reality.
